name: STACK OSL01 Ulven (ex-DigiPlex)
notes: Located in the Okern district of central Oslo; originally designed and built in 1981 for the Norwegian government as a data centre and communication hub. STACK/DigiPlex runs heat-reuse with Fortum district heating (announced 2018). No public MW capacity found.

name: DigiPlex Rosenholm
notes: One of DigiPlex's three original Oslo-area campuses (Rosenholm, Ulven, Fetsund) per trade press 2020 roundup; Rosenholm is in south-east Oslo. No public MW capacity found.

name: Telenor Oslo data center (Sigurds gate 14)
notes: Telenor-operated facility at 14 Sigurds Gate, Oslo, listed with 4.5 MW power capacity (aggregate listing).

name: Basefarm Oslo data centers
notes: Basefarm (now part of Orange Business) operates colocation data centres in Oslo, historically at Ulven. Capacity not disclosed in sources found.

name: Bulk OS-IX Oslo Internet Exchange data center
notes: Bulk's first data center in Oslo, operational since 2005; hosts the Oslo Internet Exchange (OS-IX). Bulk announced an expansion to double IT capacity for AI demand (2025).

name: Skygard OSL5
notes: Skygard OSL5 facility in Oslo (Nordliveien 21 / Hornerudveien 25, Rasta), listed at 10 MW; previously associated with Basefarm OSL5 branding. Aggregate listing.

name: Magnora Data Center / Blix AI data center (former Bankenes Betalingssentral premises)
developer: Magnora Data Center / Blix Group JV
notes: Aug 2026: Magnora Data Center and Blix Group (owner of Blix Solutions) formed a 50/50 JV to develop a new AI data center in the Oslo area, buying a business section in the former Bankenes Betalingssentral (Norwegian banks' payment clearing) building. Capacity not disclosed.

name: Nordic Hub Data Centers
notes: NHDC operates data centers in Oslo and around; founded by former Telenor, Basefarm, DigiPlex and Song Networks/TDC staff. Company page only; no capacity details.

name: Green Mountain DC1-Stavanger (SVG1-Rennesoy)
notes: Underground facility inside a former NATO ammunition store at Rennesoy near Stavanger, opened 2012; fjord-water cooling; ~22,600 sqm with 29 MW IT capacity (2024-2026 reporting). Landing point for the NO-UK subsea cable (operational 2021).

name: Google Bjerkreim data center
notes: Google plans a giant data center connected to Bjerkreim transformer station in Rogaland, with a grid application for 360 MW (power for ~200,000 households), ~18x the largest existing Lnett customer. Planned; no final investment decision reported.

name: Fjordcore Sjoholt data center (Orskog trafostasjon)
notes: In June 2025 Fjordcore Sjoholt, a Tafjord Kraft subsidiary, applied to establish a data center by Orskog transformer station in Sjoholt (Aalesund municipality, More og Romsdal). The Nordre Sunnmore agricultural office has objected that the initiative conflicts with the municipal land-use plan; early-stage. No capacity published.

name: Bitfury Norway data center (Mo Industripark)
notes: Announced 20 Mar 2018: Bitfury opened an energy-efficient bitcoin-mining data center on two sites in Mo Industripark, Mo i Rana, ~USD 35M (NOK 274M) investment, ~30 jobs; initial server farm ~42 MW on 100% renewable power. Hailed as Norway's largest data center at the time; current operational status not re-verified in this pass.

name: Arctic Circle Data Center (Mo i Rana)
developer: Mo Industripark (Arctic Circle Data Center AS)
notes: Mo Industripark's own data center venture through Arctic Circle Data Center AS, announced alongside Bitfury (~2018) as part of the park's digital push (also a Digital Norway node). Construction/operational status not confirmed in sources found.

name: T1 Energy (ex-Freyr) data center, Mo i Rana
notes: T1 Energy (the company formerly building Freyr's battery factory in Mo i Rana) has secured grid power and wants to establish a data center in the existing factory premises. Early-stage plan; capacity not disclosed.

name: Bodo data center initiative
notes: American Danny Hayes and a local Bodo team launched plans (~2 years before the report) for data centers and smart-city solutions in Bodo/Nordland and are seeking investors; the project continues without Hayes. Early stage, no capacity published. Nordland county notes that data center establishment has been a challenge for several municipalities.

name: Google Valer (Ostfold/Moss region) data center
notes: Dec 2025: Google (through grid company WS Computing AS) applied for 480 MW in power area NO1 for a data center project in the Moss region / Valer municipality, Ostfold (Viken 2020-2023 county) - power equivalent to ~200,000 households. Google confirms no final decision taken yet.

name: STACK OSL03 Fetsund (ex-DigiPlex Fetsund)
notes: DigiPlex built a data centre at Fetsund (Akershus, Viken) as part of a NOK 600M two-campus expansion (with Hobol), operational since ~2019-2020; now STACK OSL03 campus. Building footprint listed ~17,438 sq ft; total capacity not disclosed.

name: DigiPlex/STACK Hobol data center
notes: Opened Oct 2020 at Holtskogen Business Park, Hobol, Indre Ostfold (Viken); 3,200 sqm built to support 6 MW, with land for a larger campus (40,000 sqm plot plus option on 27,000 sqm).

name: DigiPlex Lillestrom data center
notes: DigiPlex opened a data centre in Lillestrom (Akershus, Viken) in September 2020, its second Norwegian facility opened that year. Capacity not disclosed.

name: Green Mountain OSL1-Enebakk (formerly DC3-Oslo)
notes: Green Mountain's Oslo-region campus at Enebakk (Viken), 20 km outside Oslo, 75,000 sqm site; campus previously branded DC3-Oslo. Three buildings on site (two ~4 MW single-tenant plus a 13.5 MW multi-tenant third, ~21.5 MW built) with line-of-sight capacity to ~93 MW at full build-out.

name: Green Mountain OSL2-Hamar (TikTok Project Clover)
notes: Heggvin, Hamar (Innlandet): campus announced March 2023 for TikTok's Project Clover European data storage; five planned buildings each up to 30 MW (campus potential ~150 MW). First building operational 2025; three of five buildings in full operation per Green Mountain (2025-2026), rest under construction.

name: Eidsiva Datasenter Gjovik
notes: Jan 2024: Eidsiva entered the data center market by acquiring the 6 MW data center at Gjovik (Innlandet), described as one of Norway's most secure, with 100% Norwegian public ownership (Innlandet municipalities + Oslo via Hafslund); also takes over its operations business.

name: Google Skien data center (Gromstul)
notes: Construction of Google's Gromstul site north of Skien started 7 Feb 2024; EUR 600M (~NOK 6.8bn) investment; ~100 direct jobs; planned operational 2026. Land (~2,000 maal) bought 2019. First phase allocated 240 MW grid capacity. Described as potentially one of the world's largest data centers.

name: Green Mountain RJU1-Rjukan (DC2-Telemark)
notes: Rjukan, Telemark (Vestfold og Telemark): hydro-powered facility in the 'cradle of hydropower', online since 2014 (7.5 MW base); campus expanded with 13,000 sqm addition at Svaddevegen; waste-heat reuse to Hima Seafood trout farm; Volkswagen Group anchor tenant. ~77 staff (~10+ per MW). Green Mountain group holds ~644.5 MW reserved and is queued for ~485 MW more in Norway (NRK).

name: Green Mountain TEL-Rjukan modular site
notes: New modular colocation site at Rjukan with 2 MW modules that can be combined to ~10 MW at Tier III or up to ~35 MW at Tier I standard; announced on Green Mountain's official site. Early/development stage.

name: Bulk N01 Campus Vennesla (Kristiansand)
notes: Bulk's N01 campus on a ~3 sq km site by Kristiansand transformer station in Vennesla (Agder), powered by hydropower; operational with phased capacity (~3 MW added 2020) and expansion toward ~300 MW AI campus; CoreWeave deploying an NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 cluster there (2025), billed as one of Europe's largest NVIDIA AI deployments.

name: Bifrost Edge Arendal data center
notes: NRK Sorlandet: Bifrost Edge presented plans to build a data center in Arendal, next to the site previously intended for a waste-handling facility. Early planning stage; capacity not disclosed.
